name: Sync

hero.title: Same signal. Now it's multiplayer, and it works offline.
hero.lede: A synced value is still a signal, backed by a CRDT. Edits from other tabs, devices and people merge, survive offline and come back after a reload, and each remote change updates only the DOM that reads it. Yjs does the merging; a relay server with per-room auth is included.

why.title: Multiplayer and offline without rewriting your app.

items.title: It is still a signal
items.text: Templates, effects and the compiler can't tell a synced signal from a local one. `title()` reads, `title.set()` writes, and only the text that shows the title updates when a peer changes it.

items.title: Concurrent edits are kept
items.text: `syncedText` and `syncedList` merge by position, so two people typing or adding cards at once both keep their work. Scalars are last-writer-wins, and the docs say so.

items.title: Offline, then caught up
items.text: `persistViaIndexedDB` keeps every edit locally; the WebSocket transport reconnects and reconciles state vectors when the network returns. `ws.synced()` tells you when you're caught up.

items.title: A relay you can secure
items.text: `createSyncServer` keeps one authoritative document per room, and runs your `authorize` hook before any data moves. From the next release it also closes cross-site browser upgrades before that hook even runs.

difference.title: Collaboration is an import, not a rewrite.

before.label: a local signal
before.caption: Lives in one tab and is gone on reload.

after.label: a synced signal
after.caption: Same reads, same writes, same component. Now shared, merged and stored offline.

demo.title: Two devices, one list. Go offline and back.
demo.text: Add items on both devices, take one offline, keep editing, then reconnect. Both sets of changes survive.

items.name: Transports
items.text: `connectViaBroadcastChannel` across tabs, `connectViaWebSocket` across devices (auto-reconnect), `connectYDocs` in memory.

items.name: Relay server
items.text: `createSyncServer` for Node and Bun, with `authorize` and attach-to-existing-server mode.

items.name: Seeds wait for the first sync
items.text: an `initial` value never overwrites a peer's real one.

items.name: Native scalars
items.text: `syncedSignal` over a `PyreonCrdtDoc` compiles to iOS and Android (strings, numbers, booleans). Experimental.

limits.title: CRDTs prevent lost updates, not conflicts
limits.text: Scalar fields are last-writer-wins, and merged text can still read oddly when two people rewrite one sentence. Use `syncedText` for strings people edit together, and show presence.

limits.title: Budget about 60 KB gzipped
limits.text: Yjs, `y-indexeddb`, `y-protocols` and the WebSocket client come with the `/yjs` entry. It stays out of apps that never import it.

limits.title: Write your `authorize` hook
limits.text: Without one the relay accepts every connection and warns in the log, even in production. Whole-document CRDTs make per-field access hard: use one room per document.

limits.title: Native covers scalars
limits.text: On iOS and Android `syncedSignal` lowers; text, lists, presence and the Yjs transports stay web, and native cross-device transport is still being built.

end.title: Ship multiplayer without a backend rewrite. Or much of a backend.

benchmarks.h: A synced keystroke in 3.8 µs. An inbound frame in 59 ns.

comingFrom.title: Keep Yjs. Drop the bridge code.
comingFrom.note: Same Yjs document underneath, so existing Yjs data and tooling still apply. `syncedSignal` replaces the observe / unobserve / snapshot bridge, and the transports and IndexedDB persistence are included.

recipes.title: A shared board with a secured relay
recipes.text: Two clients on one room converge on the title and both cards; a client with a bad token never syncs.

faq.a: For text, lists and presence, no: it is Yjs. The package adds the signal bridge, transports, persistence and a relay. A small dependency-free last-writer-wins engine (`PyreonCrdtDoc`) exists for scalars, which is the part that compiles to native.

faq.q: Do I need my own server?
faq.a: Cross-tab sync needs none (`BroadcastChannel`). Across devices you need a relay; `createSyncServer` is one, and it can attach to your existing HTTP server.
No. It keeps an in-memory document per room so late joiners catch up. Durability lives in each client's IndexedDB, or in a store you add.

faq.q: How do I test synced code?
faq.a: With `FakeCrdtDoc` and `connectFakeDocs`, which are synchronous and need no engine. For offline-reconnect behaviour, use `createYjsDoc` with `connectYDocs`.
